title: South Korea
body:
O.P.
Hi,
I'm planning to visit japan next year and planning to travel over to Korea for about 3-7 days. Not sure yet.
Can anyone recommend or give me more details on what to do and hints and tips around there? Like transportation etc.
Best to do a "tour" thing or just plan our own trip? Easy transportation? People understand english much over there?
I wouldn't mind a discussion going on this thread would be helpful. Did a quick google search and it seems like not alot of places and did a search on whirlpool and seems like people don't really recommend South Korea?
if any can help that would be great.
Thanks alot.

[User #8767613579 postsargamondWhirlpool Forums Addict] My wife didn't like korea.
Meat isn't really that big a thing (unless you are rich), and most meals are like noodles with a lot of vegetarian side dishes. (My impressions of all-you-can-eat korean bbqs are all wrong).
But that's from a food point of view, really.
[User #347492198 posts#esrsince Oct 03Whirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
NeoX writes...
people don't really recommend South Korea?
Why would they do that? I doubt half of them have even been there?
I've been there, in fact I worked there for a few years and I can say it's a fantastic place. South Korea is under this shadow which makes it look.. primitive but I can tell you Korea isn't 'bad' at all.
They are very nice to foreigners, not all can speak English but those who can are very kind.
You have lots of places to see. If you've read a recent article in the Times magazine, they did a feature article on Seoul becoming the ideal future city with so many advanced technological equipment installed in the city for public... the night view is awesome.
Lots of historical museums, and castles for you to see, and if you travel outside of Seoul, the countryside is very beautiful it just never gets the attention/is marketed to travelers.
Don't recommend you travel alone, it can get really busy and confusing. There are buses which come at ~5minute intervals in the city and they can take you anywhere really. The public transport is solid. It is not worth comparing to the system here in Sydney.
The Won, the currency, has worked itself out very nicely for the AUD, when I arrived in Seoul I had 1 AUD for 800 Won, but nowadays you get over 1000 Won for 1AUD so now is probably a good time for you to go.
There are sooo many skeptics who have absolutely no idea about South Korea and just assume it's another pov asian country which lives in terror of North korea. Trust me it isn't. South Korea is like the 15th largest economy in the world, and people here don't starve as many people believe they do because of North Korea. North and South are like totally different places.
South korea is so modern, ask people who have actually BEEN, not those who look at a country's history and judge its current state of affairs.
I did a search myself and saw a thread about korean airlines not being safe... and they talk about the terror attacks that happened a few decades ago... you know asiana airlines got 3rd place in the world airlines award in 09? asiana belongs to korea. the other korean one, KAL which is the one I used, is as safe as any airline in the world.
i look at what i wrote and i look like a bloody travel agent promoting korea. but then i lived here for 5 years and loved it. loved the country, the people, everything. try it you'll love it too.
when exactly are you going? the south korean winter is coming up.. and it snows all over the country during winter and the korean winter is nothing like our one so if you plan to visit korea next year, and next year being january/feb, then you should pack very warm. in fact you might not be able to get clothes warm enough in oz lol
[User #2124737810 postsPogiIn the penalty box] Seoul is a wonderful place, but it really pays to have a local take you around. Visiting the temples and the historical landmarks are great.
Be prepared for the cold weather, and the shopping.
NeoX writes...
Easy transportation?
I found that taxis work well, but if you find accommodation in the city centre, then you can simply walk almost everywhere.
People understand english much over there?
English is understood but not too well by everyone, best to get a phrase book if you're going at it alone, or stick to a local friend or tour guide.
South Korea is fantastic. :)

wow thanks for the inputs everyone. Keep it coming :)
I'm planning to go over there sometime late March early April. Essentially going to Japan first to see the cherry blossums and stuff. And then plan to get a ticket from Tokyo to Seoul and back to Tokyo and then Aus
Yeah reason why i started the thread was some of the post on korea in this forum is negative and I was wondering if it's worth my time to visit it if it's got nothing to do.
Hopefully this thread will be alive for awhile :)
I'll continue on my search for things to do in korea.
Also how many days do you recommend I should stay in korea? would 4 days be enough? or should I go for a bit longer?
[edit] when I say Korea I mean South Korea cos I don't think we have any intention of going to North Korea anyway.
[User #43398744 postsblinkhmeWhirlpool Enthusiast] NeoX writes...
Can anyone recommend or give me more details on what to do and hints and tips around there?
Depends on what you'd like to do I suppose. There's heaps of winter sports destinations towards the east side of S.Korea(Gangwon) :-
http://english.visitkorea.or .kr/enu/SI/SI_EN_3_6.jsp?cid =657513 http://english.vis itkorea.or.kr/enu/FU/FU_EN_15.jsp?cid=290098
I'm sure Seoul has some winter festivals lined up in the Dec/Jan period as well
http://english.tour2korea.co m/enu/FU/FU_EN_15.jsp?cid=667695
i'm heading to Seoul, Jeju and Namiseom next year. Some of the things I plan to do :- Shopping at Seoul:- Myeong Deong, Apgujeong, Namdaemun market Tourist attractions :- Coex convention center, Gyeongbokgung Palace ( there are other palaces as well but i think this is the most popular) , Lotte World (Korean theme park) , Kimchi museum, Aquarium
If you like gambling head down to Paradise Walkerhill casino, it's pretty close to this 6 star hotel (Walkerhill Seoul) which is apparently the best hotel in Seoul, there's a DFS and tons of branded retail shops
Jeju's primarily for sightseeing and food, do a google, there should be loads of info
And Namiseom is a nice one day getaway place, not too far from Seoul
Another thing I should add is that you'll want to be wary of the 10% service charge incurred on hotel rooms, this is actually exempt for tourists, so if they do charge you this, you can claim it back at the airport(where,I'm not sure yet..)
Also, there are no amenities provided for hotel rooms (I think this is for certain amenities only though like toothbrushes) due to some silly law..

[User #329224323 poststweedledeeWhirlpool Forums Addict] South Korea is amazing place, I went to see the farms and now have been back 3 time, one for a traditional wedding.
Some tips. Taxis are excellents but try and get a bus from the airport to your hotel, or a hotel near by and then taxi. Cause its a expensive trip. I learnt that the first time.
Make sure the hotel your staying at has breakfasts and meals. Otherwise you have to eat in one of the side streets. First time for me it was a bit nerving.
For politenss remove your shoes when going into your room or someones house. Its proberly the same as Japan.
One hour from Seoul, on the border with North Korea, is the village of Panmunjom (i think thats right), from here you can see N Korea. But you have to go on a offical tour to be able to access it.
Then you want to goto the hot springs. I must admit I have not had time to go and see them but I keep getting told its well worth it.

[User #36596661 postsBigManWhirlpool Enthusiast] I love South Korea! Much better than fake Japanese!
South Korean are actually very passionate people, once you know them they will be your mate forever.
There is a big Palace in the middle of Seoul (cant remember the name), really nice to experience the Korean Culture.
There are lots of things to do, when you arrive just ask your hotel concierge or the street concierge.
Awesome food, they actually use alot of spices, some spicy some not. Try the fish cake, rice roll thing on the street. It taste even better during cold winter night!
The only downside is I dont think many Korean speak good english, i was having difficulty communicating. Maybe bring a phrase book or something.
I catch Taxi everywhere, their taxi is actually quite cheap compared to ours (Sydney).
If you going with a mate, then ask your concierge about some night activities :)

[User #4819310532 postsDidNotDidTooWhirlpool Forums Addict] Seoul is massive. I can't tell you where to go as I didn't know where I was half the time, it all looks the same. But it's a good city. Go to the look out. Lum tang mountain or some like that. Go to Pusan if you can and eat Sashimi. It's yum. Gyoung Jou has some history there with the hills(dirt mounds) where dead people lay. And some ancient places like a budhist temple on a hill, the writing is in chinese from when they didn't have written korean.
Incheon is where you'll land, I it's alright, I didn't actually see much there was wasted the 2 nights I was there.
Korea is a nice country. I hope to return there some day.
Go to some Island as well if you have time. Jayju island or something like that. Meant to be beautiful and it's where a lot of honeymooners go.
